T: The power of soup compels you.
D: A mother seeks help from two priests when her daughter is possessed.
P: Serve the soup when the priests climb the stairs to Regan's room.
S: Crab meat bound with a little mayo, egg, mustard and breadcrumbs, shaped, chilled, pan-fried in butter until golden. Lemon.
Father Merrin at the dig in northern Iraq

Chris MacNeil's dinner party at the Georgetown house

Cooked king prawns on shredded iceberg in little glasses with a Marie Rose sauce of mayo, tomato sauce, lemon and hot sauce, dusted with paprika. Peel and devein 500g cooked king prawns, leaving the tails on 8 for the rims. Mix 150g whole egg mayonnaise, 3 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, the juice of half a lemon, a few drops of hot sauce and a pinch of paprika. Finely shred half an iceberg lettuce and divide between 8 small glasses. Toss the peeled prawns with half the sauce, pile onto the lettuce and spoon over the rest. Dust with paprika and hang a tail prawn and a lemon wedge on each rim.
M: the famous green, served in a bowl only
Split peas simmered 2 hours with a smoked ham hock, onion, carrot and celery, the ham picked back in, served with crusty bread. Eat it, don't throw it.
Georgetown lemon and garlic roast chicken
Chris and Regan at home in Georgetown before it all starts

Whole chicken roasted with lemon, garlic and thyme butter under the skin, with crisp roast potatoes, buttered green beans and a proper pan gravy. Heat the oven to 220C. Mash 60g soft butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves, thyme leaves and the zest of a lemon and push it under the skin of a 1.8kg chicken. Put the lemon halves inside. Toss 1kg halved potatoes in oil and salt around the bird. Roast 20 minutes, drop to 190C and roast 50 minutes more until the thigh juices run clear. Rest 15 minutes. Stir 1 tbsp plain flour into the tray juices, add 250ml chicken stock and simmer for gravy. Boil 300g green beans for 3 minutes and butter them.
W: Cocoa whisked into hot coffee, beaten into butter, sugar and eggs with buttermilk and flour, baked at 175C for 30 minutes in two tins, sandwiched and covered in a dark chocolate fudge frosting.
K: Holy water gin and elderflower fizz
Karras tests her with a flask of plain tap water

Gin, elderflower cordial and lemon shaken cold, poured clear over ice and topped with soda, a mint sprig and a thin lemon wheel in each glass. Fill a cocktail shaker with ice and add 240ml gin, 80ml elderflower cordial and 60ml lemon juice. Shake hard for 15 seconds. Strain into 4 tall glasses over fresh ice and top each with 100ml chilled soda water. Add a mint sprig and a thin lemon wheel. For the non-drinkers, swap the gin for chilled cucumber juice.

s.how: Fold 400g crab meat with 2 tbsp mayo, 1 egg, 1 tsp Dijon and 50g breadcrumbs. Shape into 8 cakes and chill 30 minutes. Pan-fry in butter until golden and serve with lemon.

s.note: Father Merrin at the dig in northern Iraq
s.how: Char an eggplant whole over a flame until collapsed, then mash with tahini, garlic and lemon. Blitz a tin of chickpeas with tahini for hummus. Serve with pickled turnips and warm flatbreads, sumac dusted over.

m.note: the famous green, served in a bowl only
m.how: Simmer 500g split peas with a smoked ham hock, an onion, 2 carrots and 2 celery sticks in 2L water for 2 hours. Pick the ham back in and season. Serve with crusty bread. Eat it, don't throw it.

w.how: Whisk 60g cocoa into 250ml hot coffee. Beat 150g butter with 300g sugar and 3 eggs, then add the cocoa, 150ml buttermilk and 250g flour with 1 tsp bicarb. Bake in two tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Cover with 200g chocolate melted with cream.
